adversarial_critique: Claude's `"Favourable"` coding is algebraically sound if—and only if—S1122 is indexed on community-level land-allocation/zoning status (`Zone of residence`), where living in an unrecognised non-zoned settlement versus the zoned periphery sharply lowers the hazard of gaining piped water (`HR = 0.14***` among owners and `0.00***` among non-owners in Table 2/3, PDF pp. 11–12) and dramatically raises the hazard of losing piped water (`HR = 15.38***` to `68.00***` in omitted Tables 5–6, PDF pp. 14–15). However, two major vulnerabilities make the study's synthesis direction genuinely `"defensible_both_ways"`. First, the authors introduce `zone of residence` as a community infrastructure control where network connection is administratively barred (`"not possible in non-zoned areas"`, PDF p. 8 / p. 1299), whereas the paper's headline life-course tenure variable (`Residence status`: `Owner/co-owner` vs. `Renting/co-renting`, which Claude itself co-extracted into `exposure_full` and `estimate_full`) points in the opposite/mixed direction: homeowners gain piped water significantly more slowly than tenants overall (Model 1a Renting `HR = 2.56***`) and in the zoned periphery (Model 1b/Table 4 Renting `HR = 2.94**`; downtown `0.88` n.s.; non-zoned `0.00***`), because acquiring affordable property typically requires moving from equipped rental housing to unserviced peripheral plots (PDF pp. 8, 15–16). Second, Claude completely omitted the co-primary second event-history analysis of piped-water *loss* (Tables 5–7, PDF pp. 14–15), where outcome polarity flips (`HR > 1` = faster loss / worse sustained access) and where homeownership increases unadjusted loss risk (`Renting HR = 0.53***` in Model 2a) before reversing in interacted Model 2b/Table 7 (`Renting HR = 6.31**` in the non-zoned periphery, while downtown `1.67^d` and zoned periphery `1.43^d` only meet `p < 0.15` and are non-significant at `p < 0.05`). Finally, Claude failed to extract numeric sample sizes (`N = 2,134` at risk / `232` events for first access; `N = 1,226` in Table 1 or `1,220` in text / `294` events for first loss) and did not note that `HR = 0.14***` in interacted Model 1b applies specifically to the `Owner/co-owner` reference stratum (Table 3, PDF p. 12).

numerical_check_note: All stored numerical estimates in `estimate_short` and `estimate_full` (`HR = 0.14***`, `3.12***`, `2.56***`, `2.94**`, `0.00***`, and descriptive access shares `48%` vs. `22%`) match the printed paper verbatim (Table 2 on PDF p. 11 / p. 1302, Table 3 on PDF p. 12 / p. 1303, and text on PDF p. 8 / p. 1299). Two provenance gaps exist: (1) because Model 1b includes `Residence status * Zone of residence` interactions, `0.14***` and `3.12***` are conditional hazard ratios for `Owner/co-owner` (the reference category of `Residence status`, shown explicitly in Table 3; for renters and other non-owners in non-zoned periphery, `HR = 0.00***`); and (2) the dossier omits numeric sample sizes (Table 1, PDF p. 7 / p. 1298: N = 2,134 persons at risk, 232 events, 255,057 person-time units for first access; N = 1,226 in Table 1 / 1,220 in text on p. 1303, 294 events, 103,963 person-time units for first loss) and omits all estimates from the co-primary piped-water loss models (Tables 5–7, PDF pp. 14–15).
polarity_or_orientation_issue: Four orientation/polarity subtleties require care: (1) `outcome_short` says `"time to first piped-water access"` while setting `outcome_polarity = "higher = better"`; longer waiting time would be worse, whereas the Cox model actually estimates the instantaneous *hazard* of gaining access (`HR > 1` = faster access = better, as noted in `coding_note`). (2) For `Zone of residence`, the model reports `Non-zoned periphery` vs. `Zoned periphery` (`HR = 0.14***`, negative log-hazard), so restating to the recognised/zoned pole (`1 / 0.14 = 7.14`) validly yields `"Favourable"`. (3) However, `exposure_full` bundles zoning with `Residence status` (`Owner/co-owner` = ref vs. `Renting/co-renting`), where `HR = 2.56***`–`2.94**` means *renting* has faster access and *ownership* (the higher-tenure pole) is `"Unfavourable"` in Model 1a and in the zoned periphery. (4) Omitted Tables 5–7 model *loss* of piped water (`HR > 1` = faster loss = worse sustained access), inverting outcome polarity relative to Tables 2–4.
